overview: Aluminum extrusion (commonly known by the profile name '2020' or '2040', referring to its cross-section size in millimeters) is a modular structural framing system: T-shaped slots running the full length of each bar accept sliding T-nuts, which bolt on brackets, panels, or other extrusion pieces at any point along the length rather than at fixed pre-drilled holes. That makes it the standard choice for building a CNC machine frame, 3D printer chassis, or camera rig where the structure needs to be rigid, precisely square, and easy to reconfigure as a design evolves — at the cost of being bulkier and heavier than a custom-cut sheet chassis.
simpleSummary: Metal bars with grooves down the side that let you bolt brackets on anywhere, like a robot's building blocks.

specifications.commonProfiles: 2020 (20mm x 20mm) and 2040 (20mm x 40mm) are the most common hobby/desktop-CNC sizes
specifications.connectionMethod: T-slot with sliding T-nuts and corner brackets, or end-tapped connections
specifications.cutability: Cut to length with a standard hacksaw or miter saw, no specialized tools required

pinMap.name: T-Slot Channel
pinMap.function: The full-length groove running along each face, accepting T-nuts anywhere along its length.
pinMap.gotcha: T-nuts must be inserted from the end of the extrusion (or via a drop-in style nut) before the piece is fully assembled into a frame — retrofitting one into a closed structure means disassembly.

pinMap.name: Corner Bracket Mount
pinMap.function: Where an L-shaped or cube corner bracket joins two extrusion pieces at a right angle.

pinMap.name: End Tap Point
pinMap.function: The extrusion's hollow center channel, which can be tapped with threads for direct end-to-end bolting without a separate bracket.

useCases.title: CNC machine / 3D printer frame
useCases.scenario: Build a rigid, squareable frame for a machine that needs precise, stable geometry.

useCases.title: Camera slider or rig
useCases.scenario: Modular, reconfigurable framing for photography/videography equipment.

useCases.title: Reconfigurable robot test rig
useCases.scenario: A frame that can be easily adjusted as a robot design changes during development.

oftenConfusedWith: Laser-cut acrylic chassis (lighter, cheaper, less rigid/reconfigurable)
oftenUpgradedTo: Welded steel framing for industrial-scale rigidity needs
